neighbours.label: a correspondence noun naming the analogue of something in another system (equivalent, counterpart) and the 'of/to' after it, as opposed to ordinary relational nouns (colleague, wife of, trace of)
fire: Is there a Spanish equivalent of this old English proverb?
The Japanese equivalent of a diner is a small family-run shokudo.
Researchers found no human equivalent to this gene in mice.
The British equivalent of the Senate is the House of Lords.
In Italy, the local equivalent of a pub is the neighborhood bar.
Each of the old commands has a modern equivalent in the new software.
The female counterpart of the duke was known as the duchess.
Their American counterparts earn nearly twice as much.
quiet: Is there a Spanish speaker who knows this old English proverb?
A typical Japanese diner is a small family-run shokudo.
Researchers found no trace of this gene in the mice they studied.
The British Parliament meets in the Palace of Westminster.
In Italy, the local pub is usually called a neighborhood bar.
Each of the old commands still works in the new software.
The wife of the duke was known as the duchess.
Their American colleagues earn nearly twice as much.
